original_test_intent: Verify the raw and decoded Processor Type enumeration for every expected SMBIOS Type 4 processor/socket record matches the approved platform roles and remains stable after reboot, rather than validating CPU model or family.
original_method: Capture all Type 4 records, retain handle/socket designation and population Status, parse raw and decoded Processor Type for each expected socket, compare the complete mapping with the approved enum baseline including Unknown/Other policy, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves the expected processor-type enum map and reboot plan. Complete record extraction and comparison are automatable.
required_inputs: Approved raw/decoded Processor Type enum per expected Type 4 record
Unknown/Other/reserved-value policy for the applicable SMBIOS version
Expected socket/designation and populated/unpopulated record map
Validated decoded/raw SMBIOS tooling and transport
safety_requirements: Read SMBIOS only; do not hotplug CPUs, alter affinity or modify firmware.
Preserve every Type 4 record, raw enum and errors; a grep list is not a record-scoped mapping.
Do not confuse Processor Type with Processor Family, Version/model string or CPU architecture.
Apply the approved policy to unpopulated-socket records and reject missing, duplicate, reserved or wrong-role enums.
Stop on mapping ambiguity, enum drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect all Type 4 records, bind them by socket/handle/population status, compare raw and decoded Processor Type against the approved per-record map and repeat after reboot.
Do not modify processor state, infer unapproved enum meanings or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the expected type enum for each socket class and Unknown/Other policy.
Resolve firmware enumeration versus platform-role discrepancies and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The label is correct, but grep loses record identity, population status and raw enum, suppresses errors and cannot prove a complete processor set.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete decoded and, when approved, raw Type 4 data with tool/errors; compare Processor Type inside each socket-designated record.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Processor Type field, Type 4 script and 10/10-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a Type 4 table keyed by socket designation and stable record identity, retaining population Status plus raw/decoded Processor Type; compare the complete map under the applicable SMBIOS enum policy before/after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 4 systems, including multi-socket and partially populated platforms.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, dmidecode/parser, BIOS, CPU and platform-recipe revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 4 Processor Type enumeration and installed tooling documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds raw-enum, per-socket and population-state provenance while separating type from family/model.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; adds completeness and invalid/reserved-enum detection.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Expected enum map and socket population policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Processor Type is a broad role classification and does not validate processor family, model or functionality.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve a supported Unknown/Other value for specific unpopulated or firmware-defined records, but must name those records and preserve raw enums; it cannot validate only one CPU.
expected_evidence: Approval, expected per-socket type enum/unsupported policy and tool/SMBIOS versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 4 table with handle/socket/status/raw/decoded type
Complete post-reboot semantic per-socket enum comparison

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and criteria consistently request Type 4 Processor Type metadata persistence; expected enum mapping is project data.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The field and enum are identifiable and read-only; missing baseline affects readiness only.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Replaces line-oriented output with complete record and raw-enum provenance.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps complete-set and enum safeguards while correcting capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates Processor Type from family/model, handles unpopulated records and adds reserved-enum policy.

review_improvement: Prevents one matching `Central Processor` line from masking missing sockets, wrong roles or invalid enum encodings and avoids conflating broad type with CPU model coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: After the project supplies its expected per-socket enum map, all extraction, normalization and reboot comparison steps are software-controlled; engineer verdict ownership remains separate.
